The card lists mum and dad, beside lowest_common_ancestor, which returns only mum." width="100%"} In a tree two nodes have exactly one lowest common ancestor (LCA), but in a general directed acyclic graph they can have several: common ancestors (nodes with a path to both, each node counting as its own ancestor) of which none lies below another. Two people can share both parents as their most recent common ancestors in a pedigree; two commits can have several merge bases (a "criss-cross merge") in a version history; two terms can have several most specific shared categories in an ontology with multiple inheritance. `lowest_common_ancestor()` picks one of them; this method returns them all. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The first node, as an integer ID or a string label. [node_2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The second node, as an integer ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The IDs of the lowest common ancestors, in ID order; empty if the two nodes have no common ancestor. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or the graph is undirected or contains a cycle. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The ancestor sets of both nodes are found by searching backward along the edges and intersected. A common ancestor is lowest exactly when none of its direct successors is also common (any common descendant would be reached through one of them), so the check costs $O(V + E)$ in all. This follows `all_lowest_common_ancestors` from NetworkX pull request #7988. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two siblings, ann and bob, share both parents, so they have two lowest common ancestors, while `lowest_common_ancestor()` returns only one of them: ::: {#7ec601c6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec family = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["mum", "dad", "ann", "bob", "grandma"]) family.add_edges( [("grandma", "mum"), ("mum", "ann"), ("mum", "bob"), ("dad", "ann"), ("dad", "bob")] ) label = family.get_label_from_id ( [label(n) for n in family.all_lowest_common_ancestors("ann", "bob")], label(family.lowest_common_ancestor("ann", "bob")), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['mum', 'dad'], 'mum') ``` ::: :::
